call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: Charger Logistics 500-Truck MOU & DaaS Economic Model
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: Chris, the 500-truck commitment with Charger Logistics is significant. Can you walk through the revenue recognition cadence for these trucks between 2027 and 2028, and how the DaaS per-mile fee structure scales relative to your initial TaaS model?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: CEO Chris Urmson explained that the Charger Logistics MOU transitions Aurora from capital-intensive fleet ownership (TaaS) to asset-light software licensing (DaaS). Charger will own and maintain the trucks, paying Aurora an ongoing software subscription and per-mile autonomy utilization fee. Delivery will phase across 2027 and 2028 along the Dallas-to-Laredo corridor, delivering high-margin recurring software revenues and unlocking hundreds of millions in cumulative value.

call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: Roush 6-Week Manufacturing Lag & Component Quality Resolution
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: David, you cited a six-week delay in the manufacturing ramp at Roush due to material availability and end-of-line testing. Are those component shortages fully behind you now, and what gives you confidence in achieving 20 trucks per week by early December?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: CFO David Maday and VP Brad Rzetelny confirmed that the initial bottlenecks were related to specialized harness connectors and sensor calibration fixtures during initial line bring-up. The engineering team redesigned the testing protocols, all tooling is now validated, and the facility is running 16 hours a day with validated inventory on-site, providing complete confidence in hitting the 20-trucks-per-week run rate in early December.

call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: Federal AV Regulatory Framework & FMCSA Warning Beacon Exemption
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: Chris, could you elaborate on the regulatory progress with USDOT's Automated Vehicles National Strategy and the recent FMCSA five-year exemption for cab-mounted warning beacons?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: Chris Urmson emphasized that federal regulatory momentum is inflecting positively. The FMCSA five-year exemption formally validates that cab-mounted automated beacons eliminate roadside hazards for commercial drivers. Furthermore, Secretary Sean Duffy and the Trump Administration's AV National Strategy establish federal safety standards and corridor interoperability, providing regulatory certainty that reinforces Aurora's multi-state commercial rollout.
